original_question: Let I be a complete intersection in K[x1, ..., xn] generated by homogeneous polynomials all of the same degree d, and suppose the quotient K[x1, ..., xn]/I has the same monomial basis as the monomial complete intersection K[x1, ..., xn]/(x1^d, x2^d, ..., xn^d). Does K[x1, ..., xn]/I satisfy the strong Lefschetz property?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly singles out the specific complete-intersection subproblem in which I is generated by homogeneous forms of a common degree d, assumes the quotient has the same monomial basis as the monomial complete intersection K[x1, ..., xn]/(x1^d, x2^d, ..., xn^d), and asks for the strong Lefschetz property rather than drifting to the broader WLP/SLP questions in Questions 2.1–2.2.
missing_details: The paper’s Section 2 has a hidden standing assumption: unless otherwise stated, the ground field K is of characteristic zero.
The ambient ring should be made explicit as the standard graded polynomial ring S = K[x1, ..., xn].
The common degree should be stated exactly as d in N.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should be quantified universally: for every n and every such complete intersection I, does the conclusion hold?
The quotient should be viewed explicitly as a standard graded Artinian K-algebra; this Artinian situation is implicit in the monomial-basis hypothesis.
The strong Lefschetz property should be defined explicitly: there exists a linear form l in S1 such that multiplication by l^k has maximal rank from (S/I)i to (S/I)i+k for all i >= 0 and k >= 1.
If one wants complete self-containment, 'has the same monomial basis as S/(x1^d, ..., xn^d)' should mean that the same residue classes of monomials form a K-basis in both quotients.
The paper does not impose any genericity hypothesis here, so the question should not be rewritten as one about general or generic complete intersections.
The paper’s formulation is specifically about SLP, not about WLP or mixed alternatives. Those broader variants belong to the neighboring Questions 2.1 and 2.2, not to the target statement itself.
refined_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let S = K[x1, ..., xn] with its standard grading, and let I ⊆ S be a complete intersection ideal generated by homogeneous polynomials all of the same degree d ∈ N. Assume that S/I has the same monomial basis as the monomial complete intersection S/(x1^d, x2^d, ..., xn^d). Must S/I satisfy the strong Lefschetz property; equivalently, does there exist a linear form l ∈ S1 such that for every i ≥ 0 and k ≥ 1 the multiplication map ×l^k : (S/I)i → (S/I)i+k has maximal rank?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Question 2.3 in Section 2 of the paper. The nearby context first fixes the standing assumption that Section 2 is over a field of characteristic zero, then presents Question 2.1 as the main open problem for complete intersections and Question 2.2 as a stepping stone, before stating Question 2.3 as the more specific unknown case. So the paper-faithful refinement is to keep the scope at Question 2.3, add the hidden characteristic-zero and standard-grading assumptions, and make the definition of SLP explicit without broadening to WLP, generic complete intersections, or other neighboring problems. The paper does not provide a separate explicit equivalent reformulation of Question 2.3 nearby, so no alternate formulation should be added.
